title: Atrial fibrillation: type, history and anticoagulation
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's atrial fibrillation and related long-term drug therapy.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for persistent AFib.

HPI
83 y.o. female presents for routine follow-up of persistent atrial fibrillation. Pt reports stable condition. Denies palpitations, syncope, or shortness of breath. Reports good adherence to rate control and anticoagulation. No concerns voiced today.

Medication List
Apixaban 5 mg BID
Metoprolol 25 mg daily
Lisinopril 10 mg daily

Exam
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Vitals: BP 128/78, HR 74 (regular), RR 16, Temp 98.6F, SpO2 98% on RA.
Heart: RRR, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Lungs: CTAB, no wheezes or rales.
Extremities: No edema, pulses 2+ bilaterally.
Neuro: NAD.

Assessment
1. Persistent AFib: Pt is currently stable on rate control.
2. Atrial fibrillation: Currently managed with apixaban for prophylaxis.

Plan
1. Continue current medications.
2. Continue apixaban as prescribed.
3. Follow up in 3 months for repeat evaluation.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
10/14/2026
explanations: Persistent atrial fibrillation, not documented as longstanding: I48.19, other persistent (HCC 238).

distractors.why: Apixaban, rivaroxaban, warfarin and similar drugs are anticoagulants (Z79.01).
